templates.title: OpenTodo
templates.name: opentodo
templates.description: Open-source, local-first task manager. Works offline and syncs every device from one small container. Source: https://github.com/pixari/opentodo

env.name: OPENTODO_SETUP_TOKEN
env.label: Setup token (optional, 16+ characters)
env.description: When set, creating the first (owner) account asks for this token, so a server others can reach cannot be claimed by a stranger. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 16

env.name: OPENTODO_BASE_URL
env.label: Public https address (optional)
env.description: The https address people open behind a reverse proxy, for example https://todo.example.com. Leave empty when you open OpenTodo by the server's address over plain http: an https value there breaks sign-in.

env.name: OPENTODO_ALLOW_SIGNUP
env.label: Open sign-up
env.description: true lets anyone who can reach the server create an account. Otherwise the owner invites people.

select.text: Open to anyone who can reach the server

env.name: OPENTODO_TRUSTED_PROXIES
env.label: Trusted proxies (optional)
env.description: Reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For is trusted for the visitor's address: IP addresses or ranges such as 192.0.2.0/24 separated by commas, or cloudflare. Set it only when every request comes through them.

templates.note: Open http://<your-host>:8080 right after deploying: the first visitor creates the owner account (paste the setup token there if you set one), and sign-up is closed after that. Everything OpenTodo stores is in the /data volume, so back that volume up. On plain http, tasks, sync and sharing work; installing the app, offline use, push notifications and passkeys need https: put a reverse proxy with a certificate in front and set the public https address. Updates: re-pull the stable image (Recreate with Re-pull image). Docs: open-todo.app/docs/self-hosting/portainer
